headline: Saturday is mild and mostly dry, then a strong windstorm and heavy rain arrive Saturday night, with high surf on the coast Sunday.
summary: As of Friday evening, the storm that brought rain and gusty wind earlier in the day has moved east of the Cascades. Showers are fading tonight, and lows will fall into the 40s. Saturday should be mostly dry across western Washington into the afternoon, with highs in the 60s, though rain may linger at times on the western Olympic Peninsula. A stronger cold front arrives Saturday evening and moves through Saturday night with a burst of steadier rain, briefly reaching 0.15 to 0.25 inch per hour along the front. The bigger concern is strong south wind. Forecasters give a 50 to 75% chance of gusts above 58 mph, the High Wind Warning threshold, and a High Wind Watch is in effect for the Grays Harbor County coast and the northern Washington coast from Saturday afternoon through late Saturday night. Most other areas can expect gusts of 30 to 45 mph from Saturday evening into early Sunday. Because many trees still have leaves, localized power outages are possible, and clogged storm drains are possible where wind and steady rain overlap, so allow extra travel time Saturday evening. On Sunday the rain turns to showers, mostly over the North Cascades and Olympics. Snow levels drop from about 7,500 feet to near 4,500 feet, so snow falls only on high mountain areas, and highs cool into the 50s. Seas of 20 to 28 feet will bring big breaking waves to the coast. A High Surf Advisory runs from 4 AM to 10 PM Sunday and could be upgraded to a warning. Razor clam diggers should be especially careful. More rain, milder temperatures, and breezy conditions follow from Monday afternoon through midweek, with more widespread rain returning late in the week. Forecasters are less certain about the pattern from Wednesday on.
changes: Early on, forecasters described Saturday night's wind only as a possibility. By afternoon they put a 50 to 75% chance on gusts above 58 mph and issued a High Surf Advisory for Sunday, and the marine Storm Watch became a Storm Warning. The evening update kept those details and added that more wind alerts may be needed elsewhere.
